issuing_body: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
title: Minn. Stat. § 8.01 — Appearance
supports: The Attorney General shall appear for the state in criminal causes in the supreme and federal courts when the state is directly interested.
In other criminal cases, the Attorney General may appear at the request of the county attorney when the Attorney General deems it proper.

The Governor may make a written request that the Attorney General prosecute a person charged with an indictable offense, in which event the Attorney General exercises all powers of a county attorney in the matter.
important_qualifications: This is general Attorney General authority and is not an exclusive catalogue of every subject-specific criminal or civil power granted elsewhere in Minnesota law.
Medicaid-specific authority under Minn. Stat. § 256B.12 is broader and should be cited directly for Medical Assistance matters.

Do not reduce Minnesota Attorney General criminal jurisdiction to the claim that the office can act only when a county attorney asks; § 8.01 itself also contains a Governor-request pathway, and other statutes grant direct subject-matter authority.
